sourceArticle.title: Gemini Omni: AI Video Generation Inside Gemini
sourceArticle.author: Vasu Deo Sankrityayan

athenaOutput.directive: Integrate Gemini Omni as a native visual synthesis component governed by the Creative Liberation Engine's DAG, transforming raw intent into fully orchestrated, multi-scene cinematic pipelines stored directly on sovereign infrastructure.
athenaOutput.rationale: Per Article XXIII, Gemini Omni is a component, not the architecture. We must not simply build a 'wrapper' UI for prompt-to-video. Instead, we must embed Omni's native video generation capabilities deep within our agentic workflows. By utilizing DIRECTOR to break down narratives into a dependency graph of scenes, PALETTE to enforce visual consistency, and NAS-based FFmpeg pipelines to stitch the final artifact, we achieve true automated cinematic production. This fulfills Article IX (Complete Implementations) and Article XX (Zero Human Wait Time) while maintaining Article I (Sovereignty) over the final assets.

options.title: DAG-Driven Storyboard & Stitch Pipeline
options.description: DIRECTOR agent parses a creative brief into a multi-node DAG. Each node represents a specific shot or scene. SIGNAL interfaces with the Gemini Omni API to generate the video for each node in parallel. Once all nodes resolve, a backend NAS process automatically stitches, color-grades, and applies audio, delivering a complete, production-ready video file.
options.tradeoffs: High architectural complexity in managing parallel asynchronous video generation and ensuring temporal consistency between shots. However, it delivers a truly 'complete' artifact rather than fragmented clips.

options.title: Sovereign B-Roll & Texture Factory
options.description: An automated background daemon that uses Omni to continuously generate high-quality, brand-aligned B-roll, transitions, and environmental textures based on PALETTE's guidelines. These assets are automatically downloaded, tagged by KEEPER, and stored on the NAS for instant use by human editors or Broadcast Hive agents.
options.tradeoffs: High initial API compute costs and storage requirements on the NAS. Yet, it aggressively builds sovereign creative capital (Article I) and eliminates future wait times for asset retrieval.

options.title: Real-Time Broadcast Engine Integration
options.description: Embed Gemini Omni directly into the Broadcast Hive (ATLAS, GRAPHICS, CONTROL_ROOM). Omni generates dynamic, context-aware visual overlays or transitional videos on the fly during live streams or dynamic presentations based on audience sentiment or live data feeds.
options.tradeoffs: Latency is the primary risk; live video generation must be fast enough to not disrupt the broadcast flow. Massive 'wow' factor and unparalleled dynamic capability if latency constraints are met.

options.title: Interactive Visual REPL (Antigravity Canvas)
options.description: A frontend Antigravity IDE extension where creatives can write narrative code or structured prompts and instantly see the Omni video render in a side-panel. It bridges the gap between code/spec and visual output, acting as an ultra-fast prototyping environment.
options.tradeoffs: Requires heavy frontend state management and API bridging. It leans slightly toward 'human-in-the-loop' which borders on violating Article XX if not designed as a strictly optional ideation tool.

options.title: Cloud-Based Biometric Video Synthesis
options.description: Using Gemini Omni to generate lifelike videos of specific, real human actors or team members based on reference photos passed to the Google Cloud API.
options.tradeoffs: Directly violates Article XXIV (Biometric Data Sovereignty). We cannot send real human biometric data to a cloud API. Any human generation must be strictly limited to synthetic/fictional personas.
